data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test that pins an exact artifact count violates the Open\u2013Closed Principle (OCP): the module under test should be open to accepting new evidence (extension) but closed to arbitrary modification. Instead of asserting N == fixed_count, the test should assert an invariant that holds across all legitimate extensions \u2014 e.g., every committed artifact satisfies validation, provenance, and integrity constraints, and the count remains within a domain-defined boundary.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system is a closed-world registry where no new artifacts are ever legitimately admitted, exact-count assertion may be appropriate","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the invariant is too weak (e.g., 'count > 0'), it may pass even when most artifacts are corrupt","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If legitimate new evidence can itself be malformed and still be committed, the invariant must include validation of the evidence-acceptance pathway, not just the committed artifact","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal mechanism: new evidence arrives as a legitimate, well-formed extension to the artifact set. The exact-count assertion has no causal link to correctness \u2014 it only detects whether mutation occurred, conflating expected extension with unexpected corruption. An invariant-based assertion causally targets the property that actually matters: each artifact's validity. When new evidence arrives, the invariant still holds because the evidence is legitimate; when corruption occurs, the invariant breaks because the artifact is malformed, regardless of count.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
